Subject: Possible auth anomaly during this morning's tabletop — can you confirm IRP handoff?

Hi Naomi,

We observed an uptick in token validation failures and a handful of 503s against the Redwood inference endpoint during our scheduled tabletop this morning (approx 08:50–09:10 PDT). It looked transient on our side but the timing overlapped with the session where we exercised session token rotations.

Can you confirm whether Redwood saw any correlated errors and, if so, provide:
- Immediate telemetry excerpts (redacted) for the window 08:40–09:20 PDT
- Incident response plan (IRP) summary for this event and any SOC2/SIG/CAIQ evidence we can include in our audit notes
- An estimated ETA for a post-incident write-up — FinConnect compliance needs a short summary within 48 hours.

We did a quick tabletop today and want to capture artifacts while it's fresh. Please loop in whoever owns forensics and SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Tom

Subject: Evidence bundle for FinConnect tabletop incident (SUP-1284)

Tom — attaching the initial evidence bundle as discussed.

Attachments included (redacted where appropriate):
- incident_logs.zip (sanitized application & gateway logs, 08:30–09:30 PDT)
- telemetry_excerpt.csv (aggregated token validation metrics & error traces)
- IR_playbook_v2.pdf (excerpted runbook steps we executed)
- SOC2_evidence_index.xlsx (mapping of artifacts to control IDs)

Summary of what we found (high level):
- Between 08:48–08:55 PDT we saw a short spike in token validation errors originating from an edge cache misconfiguration following a third-party identity provider's key rotation.
- The runtime rejected a small percentage of token refresh attempts due to stale cache entries; requests retried and the overall client impact was low, but the tabletop exposed the timing mismatch.
- Containment: edge cache TTL rolled back and a cache invalidation was applied at 08:58 PDT. Full mitigation completed 09:02 PDT.

Notes: logs have user identifiers redacted per our customer data handling policy. If your compliance team requires raw logs, let Naomi know and we can discuss a temporary, tightly scoped data share under an addendum.

Subject: FinConnect post-incident report & next steps (SUP-1284)

Tom — adding the formal post-incident summary and next steps. Attached: redwood_postmortem_20270521.pdf (concise write-up) and we left the previous evidence bundle in the Drive folder.

Executive summary (short):
- Root cause: timing mismatch between Redwood's edge cache TTL and a third-party IdP key rotation; stale cache entries caused token validations to fail for a small percentage of requests during 08:48–08:55 PDT.
- Impact: ~0.8% increase in token validation failures for affected clients during the window; no persisted data loss; retries succeeded for most requests.
- Mitigation: manual cache invalidation at 08:58 PDT; TTL rollback and automated invalidation script deployed at 09:02 PDT.

Corrective actions (owner / ETA):
- Automated IdP rotation detector and preemptive cache invalidation (Sean Gallagher / 2 weeks)
- Add an IdP rotation coordination check to our deployment runbooks and SOC2 evidence mapping (Marissa Cole / 1 week)
- Expand telemetry to include rotation-flagged metrics for faster detection (Platform / 3 weeks)

SLA & credits: if FinConnect would like us to evaluate an SLA credit, please open a billing ticket referencing SUP-1284 and Naomi or I will coordinate the review.

We understand the importance of preserving artifacts for audits; the SOC2_evidence_index.xlsx maps each artifact to control IDs and contains a redaction log. If you need a signed attestation or additional signed evidence, let us know.

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_20270521.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finconnect-evidence
